body:
`insight:lender-blowup-signals` | 2026-11-19 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Financials need their own tests (IL&FS, DHFL, Yes Bank, RCap, Lehman, SVB, Credit Suisse): (1) Funding: share of CP/short-term wholesale funding; ALM gap in the 1-year bucket (DHFL, IL&FS); uninsured/bulk deposit share and depositor concentration (SVB ~90%+, Yes Bank low CASA). (2) Asset quality: RBI divergence disclosures (Yes Bank FY16-17), restructured + SMA-2 book, loans to promoter-group or 'general purpose corporate loans' (RHFL), wholesale/developer concentration. (3) Growth: loan growth >30%/yr for several years in corporate books. (4) Capital: leverage (Lehman ~30x; NBFCs >7-8x), Level 3/model-marked assets vs equity, fair-value of HTM securities vs equity (SVB losses ~= equity). (5) Market: CP/bond spread spikes, CDS (Credit Suisse Oct 2022), rating outlooks; (6) Governance: regulator actions on CEO (Yes Bank), auditor exits (RCap PwC), material weakness opinions (CS), CRO vacancies (SVB). (7) Window-dressing: quarter-end vs average balance sheet (Repo 105). Rule: a lender trading at a discount to book with any two of these is pricing hidden losses -- avoid; equity is a thin slice (10x leverage means a 10% asset loss wipes it).

**Links:** part_of -> `insight:disqualifiers`, about -> `insight:avoid-ruin`
**Sources:** <https://www.icaew.com/insights/viewpoints-on-the-news/2023/mar-2023/chart-of-the-week-silicon-valley-bank> ; <https://www.isas.nus.edu.sg/papers/yes-bank-in-moratorium-how-it-collapsed-and-what-next> ; <https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/wall-street-abuzz-over-lehman-autopsy-report>

- Promoters: Samayat Services LLP (an SPV of Kedaara Capital and Partners Group) and Kedaara Capital Fund II LLP `[UDRHP]`. Pre-IPO stake was 96.55%.
- Sell-downs (screener promoter %): IPO Dec-2024, a pure ₹8,000 cr OFS, 28.7× subscribed → 74.55%. Jun-2025 block of 19.36%, ₹10,220 cr → 54.2%. Early 2026, 14% bulk deal of ₹7,635 cr at ₹117 (an 8% discount) → **40.0% (Sep-26)**. Total realised ≈ **₹25,855 cr**, none of it to the company.
- Absorbed by DIIs (9.9% → 36.5%) and FIIs (6.6% → 18.8%). Retail holders fell from 9.33 lakh to 6.43 lakh `[SCR]`.
- Supply overhang ≈ 40% × ₹42,852 cr ≈ ₹17,000 cr at CMP. At 1–1.5 blocks a year that is 2–3 more years of periodic supply. Management says the sponsors "intend to remain invested for the long term" `[HSIE]`. PE sponsors exit by design, so that statement should be treated as unverified.
- **Pledge: 0** `[HSIE]`.

body:
- Margin promises are reliable: 'sustain ~28.6%' (Aug-25) -> FY26 30.4%; every quarter since is >=30.5% on screener.
- Near-term capacity was nearly on time (10,000-t press Q4FY26 as promised; 4,000-t press one quarter late, acknowledged).
- Big-project dates are not: the INR 650 cr heavy-component plant went from 'finished by Q2-Q3 FY27' (Aug-25) to 'commence operation in Q4 FY2028' (Nov-26) while every call in between said it was on schedule. That is the clearest silent goalpost move in this peer set.
- Also missed: a US PV programme ramp promised for Nov-Dec 2025 began in Q1-Q2 FY27; a hoped-for acquisition 'in 6-8 months' never came up again.
title: HAPPYFORGE › 3. Reading

body:
- **Volunteered vs prompted:** Coforge 100% volunteered (n=2) vs 79% prompted (n=8). Mphasis 50% volunteered (n=6) vs 100% prompted (n=2). There is no consistent sign, as in auto components. Too small to test.
- **Precise vs vague:** Coforge precise 100% / range 75% / vague 67%. KPIT precise 100% / vague 75%. Mphasis's one precise promise (Logistics "from Q3") missed. Weakly in the expected direction for two of three companies; specificity stays a weight, not a signal.
- **Guidance refusers:** Persistent ("we don't give forward-looking guidance") and, since FY25, KPIT on revenue. Their scores rest on aspirations and growth-shape statements, so read their 95–100% scores with that in mind.

**Walk log (every skip and why):**
| # | Symbol | Mcap ₹ cr | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | NRBBEARING | 4,142 | **skip** | PEAD avoid window. Q2 FY27 SUE −0.09 ≤ cut-point −0.001 → **quintile 2** (event 04-Nov-2026, inside the 63-trading-day window that starts 20-Aug-2026). Computed with `live_tracker.sue_for` on `eps_history.csv` and the fixed `sue_cutpoints.json`. |
| 2 | VSTIND | 3,294 | **skip** | PEAD avoid window. Q2 FY26 EPS was missing from eps_history, so I added it from the NSE integrated XBRL (EPS 6.79, filed 29-Oct-2025) and bonus-adjusted the pre-Oct-2024 EPS for the 10:1 bonus (shares 1.544 → 16.986 cr). Q2 FY27 SUE **−1.30 → quintile 1** (event 28-Oct-2026). |
| 3 | HINDWAREAP | 1,308 | **skip** (judgment, see note) | Passed the mechanical hard filters: no promoter encumbrance (SHP 30-Sep-2026 XBRL), PEAD Q3 (SUE +0.06), solvency not red (S2 interest cover 1.17x and S3 fired, but India grade = S1 or S5 = blank). Same-day CEO/CFO/CS exits were explained as transfers to the subsidiary Hindware Ltd. **But** NCLT Kolkata sanctioned (14-Oct-2026, certified copy 06-Nov-2026) a composite scheme. Under it the consumer business is demerged into HHIL Ltd and the rest of the listed company is **amalgamated into Hindware Ltd, and HINDWAREAP is dissolved**. The scheme becomes effective on ROC filing, and the record date is pending. The subject cannot be scored through 2027-09-30, which is the whole purpose of the run. |
| 4 | **SUNFLAG** | 6,643 | **SUBJECT** | Passed every check (section 1): no promoter encumbrance, no qualified audit and no auditor exit (rotation after a 5-year term), PEAD **quintile 4** (Q2 FY27 SUE +1.04, event 13-Nov-2026), solvency screen 0 flags, no fraud-judgment flags found. |

**Deviation note (for the user/caller to accept or reverse).** Skipping HINDWAREAP adds a rule that was not in the task: *"the
listed entity must not be scheduled to cease to exist before the call horizon."* It is objective and it was decided before
SUNFLAG was looked at, but it is still a deviation. If it is rejected, the subject would be HINDWAREAP, and the calls would have to be written on
the successor shares.
**Tool note.** On 23-Nov-2026 `nse_fetch.py pledge` returned **0 rows for every symbol**. That includes INDOTECH, which had data on 21-Nov. So promoter
encumbrance was read from the latest **SHP XBRL** instead (`WhetherAnySharesHeldByPromotersAreEncumbered…` flags). The scoreboard's
`sources.py` already handles this transient empty answer.
